author: Elastic
attributes.description: Detects Vertex AI GenerateContent requests that set safety_settings.threshold to BLOCK_NONE. That threshold disables category blocking for the listed harm categories when clients explicitly send safetySettings. Attackers and careless apps use BLOCK_NONE to weaken built-in Gemini filters.
false_positives: Approved research projects that document BLOCK_NONE for evaluation. Prefer labeled service accounts and exclude those principals.
attributes.name: GCP Vertex AI Safety Filters Set to BLOCK_NONE
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating GCP Vertex AI Safety Filters Set to BLOCK_NONE

The GenerateContent request set `safety_settings.threshold` to `BLOCK_NONE` for one or more harm
categories. Category blocking is disabled for those categories (the model may still refuse in text,
but built-in filters will not stop generation for that category). Attackers and misconfigured apps
use this to weaken Gemini safety controls.

#### Possible investigation steps

- Confirm which categories were set to BLOCK_NONE via
  `full_request.safety_settings.category` and `threshold` on the alert.
- Read the prompt text. Look for disallowed content that would normally be blocked.
- Hunt the same `cloud.project.id` / model for subsequent HIGH/MEDIUM safety ratings or unusual
  successful completions after filters were weakened.
- Identify the caller via auditlogs GenerateContent (`source.ip`, `client.user.email`).
- Check whether org policy or an approved wrapper SDK requires stricter defaults
  (BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE or higher).

### False positive analysis

- Documented research or red-team projects that intentionally use BLOCK_NONE. Prefer labeled service
  accounts and exclude those principals.

### Response and remediation

- Require stricter thresholds via org policy, admission control, or application defaults; revoke
  non-compliant callers.
- If abuse is confirmed, rotate credentials and review other config changes (including
  SetPublisherModelConfig) by the same actor.
attributes.query:
from logs-gcp_vertexai.prompt_response_logs-* metadata _id, _version, _index
| where
    data_stream.dataset == "gcp_vertexai.prompt_response_logs" and
    MV_CONTAINS(gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_request.safety_settings.threshold, "BLOCK_NONE")
| keep
    _id,
    _version,
    _index,
    @timestamp,
    cloud.project.id,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.model,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.api_method,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_request.contents.parts.text,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_request.safety_settings.category,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_request.safety_settings.threshold,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_response.candidates.finish_reason,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_response.candidates.safety_ratings.category,
    gcp.vertexai.prompt_response_logs.full_response.candidates.safety_ratings.probability
attributes.setup:
## Setup

Requires prompt_response_logs with full_request.safety_settings.threshold. The field is only present when the client
sends safetySettings on the GenerateContent request.
